newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh power shortfall triggers clashes.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh power shortfall triggers clashes.

text.p: At least 10 people were injured in clashes triggered by a power shortfall in Bangladesh that has shut down industries and disrupted irrigation, officials and press reports said on Tuesday.
The violence erupted on Monday after an unprecedented power crisis that the government said was caused by "sabotage" of the national power grid.
An angry mob protesting frequent power cuts in the southeastern town of Magura on Monday attacked the house of an electricity engineer and burned his car, the Bangladesh Observer reported on Tuesday.
At least 10 people, including five policemen, were injured as they tried to rescue the engineer and his family, it said.
Meanwhile, thousands of farmers in the northern rice growing district of Thakurgaon besieged the office of the district commission for several hours on Monday, local officials told reporters.

On March 14 two supply towers of the country's power grid collapsed, leading to outages. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Sunday said the damage reflected plans to sabotage her development programmes. She did not name any suspects.
"Government agencies detected the power-tower collapse as an act of sabotage. Experts found nuts, bolts and plates displaced," the Energy Ministry said in a statement on Monday.
"This had badly affected irrigation as thousands of water pumps failed to operate for two days," said Matiur Rahman, a journalist in the northern district of Dinajpur.
A makeshift arrangement restored the region's power supply on Monday, he said.
Officials blamed the power shortfall in recent months on dwindling gas supply to generation plants.
Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan told a news conference on Saturday that electricity generation was suffering due to a shortfall in the gas supply to power plants.
The country was now producing 1,650 megawatts against a minimum demand of 2,200 megawatts, energy officials said.
The Financial Express on Tuesday quoted a leading trade body as saying factories were losing 22 percent of total working hours due to power cuts in recent weeks.
"The situation in industries is very very critical," the newspaper quoted A.S.M. Quasem, President of the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry, as saying.
